title: Cool Vacations!
pages: Book p.80 to 89 · Workbook p.64 to 71

learn.title: Welcome to Unit 8: Cool Vacations!
lines: In this unit you will:
🏖️ learn words for vacations and travel: camping, ruins, theme park, passport, suitcase
💭 imagine with the second conditional: If I went on safari, I would take photos.
⚖️ choose with would rather: I'd rather go camping than stay at a hotel.
🎵 sing a song, 📖 read about tree house vacations, 🙏 be a respectful tourist, ✍️ write a travel review

sections.pages: Book p.82 to 83 · Workbook p.64 to 65

learn.title: What kind of vacation do you enjoy? (short summary)
lines: Read the full texts on pages 82 and 83 in your book.
🏕️ Like quiet places? Go camping. Sleep in a tent under the stars.
🦁 Like nature? Go on a photo safari. Take pictures of wildlife with a guide.
🏛️ Like history? See the ruins of an old city, or take a tour of a modern city.
🏨 Want to relax? Stay at a big hotel and swim at the beach.
🎢 Love fun? Buy a ticket for a ride at a theme park!

sections.title: Grammar 1: Second conditional

learn.title: Imagine! Things that are not real now 💭
lines: Use the second conditional to talk about an imagined situation.
Real: I don't live near a beach, so I can't go swimming every day.
Imagined: If I lived near a beach, I would go swimming every day.

learn.title: If + past, would + verb
learn.note: I'd = I would. With be, use were for everyone: If I were…, If she were…
table: If we went on a photo safari,
I would take pictures of lions.
he would buy a new bike.

learn.title: You can start with either part
lines: If you start with If, put a comma.
examples: I'd go mountain climbing if I weren't afraid of heights.
He wouldn't spend all of his time in museums if he didn't like art.
If you had a lot of money, where would you go on vacation?

sections.title: Grammar 2: Would rather

learn.title: would rather = would prefer ⚖️

learn.title: Tree houses in India 🇮🇳
lines: Read the full text in your book. This is a short summary.
In India, there are tree houses 27 meters (90 ft.) up in the air!
They are made from natural and recycled materials. The electricity comes from the sun.
A bamboo elevator, powered by water, carries you up. You walk to your neighbor on a rope bridge!
You can visit caves and go on a photo safari to see elephants.

learn.title: Tree houses in Peru 🇵🇪
lines: In Peru, you can stay in a tree house near the Yarapa River in the Amazon rain forest.
The tree houses are connected by passageways and bridges.
You can watch people fish, see a river dolphin, and see monkeys looking for food!
🌙 Weird but true: A company is planning future vacations on the moon!

learn.title: The Forbidden City (Workbook p.70)
lines: Read the full text in your workbook. This is a short summary.
The Forbidden City in Beijing, China, was built for the emperor. Building began in 1406 and finished in 1420.
Fires burned buildings in 1557, 1597 and 1644, but they were rebuilt.
No one could enter without the emperor's invitation. A tall wall and a river protected it.
It opened as a museum in 1925, and became a World Heritage Site in 1987.

learn.title: Our mission: Be a respectful tourist 🙏
lines: A respectful tourist follows the rules and cares about the people and places they visit.
The photo on page 89 shows a mosque in Singapore. People take off their shoes before they go in.

learn.title: Joseph Lekuton, National Geographic Explorer
lines: Joseph Lekuton is a teacher.
His message: Meeting people from other cultures helps us understand each other. Education and travel are the best teachers. Read his words on page 89. 📖

learn.title: How to be a respectful tourist
lines: 👟 Take off your shoes when people ask you to.
👕 Wear polite clothes at temples.
🗣️ Learn to say hello and thank you in the local language.
🚯 Don't drop trash. Keep places clean.
📷 Ask before you take photos of people.

book.q: Is tourism a good thing for a place? Is it a good thing for local people?
book.answer: Yes, it can be. Tourists bring money and jobs. But too many tourists can make places dirty and crowded.

book.q: How should tourists show respect for the places they visit?
book.answer: They should follow the rules, wear polite clothes, and keep the places clean.

book.q: Compare your ideas with a partner or group. Which ideas does everyone like best?
book.answer: Everyone likes the idea: don't drop trash, and say thank you in the local language.

sections.title: Writing: A Travel Review

learn.title: What is a travel review?
lines: A travel review tells about someone's vacation. It helps other people decide if they want the same trip.
Use different kinds of sentences to make it interesting:
✏️ short sentences: We saw a stingray, too!
🔗 long sentences: We had to swim to the island and walk up the rocks.
❓ questions and ❗ exclamations: Delicious!

learn.title: Review of the Antigua Ecotour (short summary)
lines: Read the full review in your workbook. 📒
The writer went on an ecotour in Antigua. The guides took them by boat to a rock bridge, then snorkeling at a coral reef.
They saw colorful fish and a stingray. Snorkeling was hard work, but it was worth it!

learn.title: Plan your travel review
lines: 1. Where did you go? Ask a question to start: Do you like beaches?
2. What did you see and do?
3. What did you like? What didn't you like?
4. Would you recommend it? This is the trip for you!

wb.q: Underline a sentence that describes just one idea.
wb.answer: We saw a stingray, too!
wb.hint: Look for a short sentence. (Other answers: We saw many colorful fish. / Delicious!)

wb.q: Circle another sentence that describes more than one idea.
wb.answer: We had to swim to the island and walk up the rocks and through a cave.
wb.hint: Look for a long sentence with "and."

wb.q: Write a review of a vacation. Tell what you liked and didn't like. Describe what you saw and did. Use different types of sentences.
wb.answer: Do you like the beach? Then visit Koh Samet! We swam in clear water and ate fresh fish. The sand was white and soft. The boat trip was a little long, but it was worth it. This is the trip for you!
wb.hint: Use the plan in Learn: start with a question and end with an exclamation!

sort.title: What kind of sentence is it?
items: We swam to the island and walked up the rocks.

This is the trip for you!
